text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bracing for the flood of a century: Crisis reveals towns' planning.
- Head for dry land, 17,000 in towns told: Winnipeg residents may be in danger.
- Net rumour sends Bre-X on wild ride.
- PM wants 'to go to the people.' Rhetoric heats up as Ottawa takes on election-campaign atmosphere.
- Guerrilla handed Fujimori reason to attack: Canadian ambassador says rebel leader made fatal move to press demands.
- Bre-X shares sent on wild ride: Stock gains, loses $1.2 billion in minutes on false report of Freeport president quitting.
- Freeport tests still lack gold: analysts.
- An era ends as TSE closes trading floor after 145 years: Champagne, confetti mark final move to computerized dealing.
- Busang drill results spark Bre-X trading frenzy.
- Tighter rules for funds: Industry set to bring in mandatory code.
